facts.name: Sensitive Fern
facts.light: Part sun to full shade; more sun only if the soil stays wet
facts.notes: A coarse, light green fern with broad, wavy-edged fronds, unlike the lacy look of most ferns. The fronds collapse at the first frost (that's the 'sensitive'), leaving stiff brown bead-like spore stalks that stand all winter. Spreads by roots into a groundcover, quickly in wet spots. Deer leave it alone.
facts.toxSrc: UT Extension notes it is toxic to horses and livestock

sources.note: MSU prairie fen fact sheet for a native fern of Michigan's wet areas; 6 to 30 in, shade tolerant.

sources.title: PerennialReference.com (Hallson Gardens): Onoclea, sensitive fern
sources.note: 12 to 30 in; part sun to full shade, more sun if kept constantly wet; average to rich, acidic, moist to wet soil; zones 3 to 8. A vigorous spreader along ponds and streams, about as controlled as other spreading ferns in average gardens.

sources.title: UT Extension Tennessee Yards: Onoclea sensibilis
sources.note: Toxic and sometimes fatal to horses and livestock.
